summary.whatChanges: The minimal (and agent) reporter no longer hardcodes `silent: 'passed-only'`. It now tracks whether the user explicitly provided a `silent` option in config/CLI and only applies its `passed-only` default when none was given, applying it at init time instead of in the constructor.
behaviorChanges: Running with the minimal/agent reporter and an explicit `silent: false` now prints logs from both passing and failing tests instead of suppressing passed-test output.
An explicit `silent: true` is now honored by the minimal/agent reporter, suppressing all test logs.
Without an explicit `silent` setting, the minimal/agent reporter still defaults to 'passed-only'.
Resolved config now exposes a `providedOptions.silent` boolean indicating whether `silent` was user-specified.
risks: Users who relied on minimal/agent suppressing passed-test logs while setting `silent: false` globally for other purposes will now see extra console output.
The silent default is now set in onInit rather than the constructor, so any code reading `reporter.silent` before initialization sees `undefined`.
Detection relies on `source.silent != null`, so an explicitly passed `silent: undefined` is treated as not provided.
